subject: RapidStream unexpected usage spike — request for attribution & provisional credit
messages:
From: RapidStream Ops <ops@rapidstream.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Unexpected billing spike after switching to streaming endpoint

Hi Sergio,

We rolled RapidStream's inference traffic to your new /v2/stream endpoint on Nov 15 to reduce latency. Since then our bill has shown a ~3x increase for Nov 15–17 compared to baseline. We didn’t change traffic patterns, only the endpoint.

Can you help explain how streaming vs. non-streaming calls are metered? Our finance lead (cc'd) is escalating — we need usage attribution and a breakdown by model and request id. If this looks like an over-count, we will request a credit.

Account ID: RS-88-ALPHA
Invoice referenced: INV-20261115

Attached: invoice snapshot (invoice_202611.pdf) — happy to share any logs you need.

Thanks,
Elena Kozlova
Head of Ops, RapidStream.ai

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: RapidStream Ops <ops@rapidstream.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Unexpected billing spike after switching to streaming endpoint

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and for the invoice. I’m escalating to our billing team and AM ops so we can get you a quick attribution.

Two quick asks to speed triage:
1) Can you share 1–2 example request IDs (the UUID in your app logs) for calls made on Nov 16?
2) Do you have sample request/response sizes (tokens or characters) around those calls?

Ben and Marissa — assigning this to you for a usage audit. RapidStream is a strategic self-serve account; they report no traffic pattern change and only switched endpoints. Please prioritize.

I’ll follow up with a provisional timeline by EOD tomorrow.

— Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0500
Subject: FWD: Unexpected billing spike after switching to streaming endpoint

Forwarding RapidStream's note and invoice. Key context: their deploy on Nov 15 to /v2/stream produced a 3x consumption jump on our metering export for Nov 15–17; they insist traffic volume did not change.

What I pulled from the portal so far:
- Account: RS-88-ALPHA
- Plan: Standard (pay-as-you-go)
- Billing contact supplied invoice INV-20261115

Requested action: please run a token-level attribution for Nov 14–18 with grouping by endpoint and model. If the streaming endpoint increments internal per-frame tokens (prefix splitting) we should identify that and confirm whether we double-counted prefix vs. streaming frames. If you need their sample request IDs, ping Elena.

Thanks — Sergio

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:40:00 -0500
Subject: Re: FWD: Unexpected billing spike after switching to streaming endpoint

Adding my notes after an initial pass on the telemetry:

- Preliminary finding: there is a burst of short streaming sessions Nov 15–17 where the runtime emitted multiple partial responses per request. Those partials were logged as separate token batches in one of our legacy aggregation lanes. That lane should have been reconciled by the new de-duplication pass, but a sync gap affected ~0.9% of accounts during the release window. RapidStream's traffic pattern (many tiny streaming frames) amplified the effect.

- Next steps I need from the account: two example request IDs + the invoice you already attached (INV-20261115) so I can crosswalk server-side traces to the billing ledger.

- Provisional remediation: if this is the anomaly we can: (a) remove duplicate partial batches and recalc tokens for the window, and (b) issue a provisional credit while we finish the audit. I recommend a provisional credit of $2,500 pending confirmation; final adjustment to follow after the audit.

I attached a sanitized sample usage export for the window (usage_export_sample.csv) and a short internal checklist. Marissa — can you prepare the provisional-credit form if Ben confirms?

— Ben Carter
Billing Ops Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: RapidStream Ops <ops@rapidstream.ai>, Elena Kozlova <elena@rapidstream.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Unexpected billing spike after switching to streaming endpoint

Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround. Ben confirmed a release window sync gap that likely inflated counts for accounts with many short streaming frames (your case). Our ask: please send 2–3 example request IDs from Nov 16 and a short sample of request/response sizes (token counts if you capture them). Once we receive the IDs we will: 

1) Reconcile server traces to the billing ledger (Ben)
2) Remove duplicate partial-batch entries for the window where found
3) Issue a provisional one-time credit of $2,500 against INV-20261115 while we complete the audit (final delta subject to adjustment)

Attachments: provisional_credit_form.pdf (signed by your billing contact will speed processing), and a sanitized usage export we used for the initial check (usage_export_sample.csv).

If you'd like, we can set up a 30-minute call Monday to walk through the reconciliation live.

Cheers,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0198
